intended_seat: Head of the finance function in a mid market or family owned business, reporting to the owner, CEO or a group CFO. Owns accounting, cash, compliance and the audit. Often the first professional finance hire.
notes: Weights sum to 100. Anchors describe evidence, not people. Edit weights and anchors before lock; do not add criteria that touch personality, health, or protected characteristics.

criteria.name: Accounting and reporting under IFRS
criteria.anchor_1: Produces a trial balance but cannot map it to a full set of IFRS statements or explain the notes. Relies on the auditor to draft the statements.
criteria.anchor_3: Has prepared a full IFRS set with notes for an entity of similar size, can explain the main judgments, and has taken the statements through audit with limited adjustments.
criteria.anchor_5: Prepares audit ready statements with a working file the auditor can follow, explains the entity's judgment areas without prompting, and has handled a first year IFRS adoption or a group reporting package.
evidence_sources: work sample: a set of statements or notes they prepared
questions: Walk me through the last set of financial statements you prepared: which notes carried judgment and how did you support them?
What were the auditors' adjustments last year, and which of them should you have caught?
Our business has [inventory / long term contracts / related parties]. What would you look at first?

criteria.name: Month end close and reporting cadence
criteria.anchor_1: Reports quarterly or when asked. Cannot describe a close calendar or the reconciliations performed each month.
criteria.anchor_3: Runs a monthly close to a calendar, reconciles bank, receivables, payables and intercompany every month, and delivers a management report by a fixed working day.
criteria.anchor_5: Runs a close inside ten working days with a documented checklist, has shortened it in a previous role, and produces a management pack the owner reads and acts on.
evidence_sources: work sample: close checklist or management pack
questions: What does your month end look like day by day?
Which reconciliations do you insist on every month, and which have you seen skipped elsewhere with consequences?
What is in your management pack and what does the owner do with it?

criteria.name: Cash, working capital and treasury discipline
criteria.anchor_1: Cannot produce a cash forecast or explain the drivers of working capital. Treats cash as the bank balance.
criteria.anchor_3: Maintains a rolling 13 week cash forecast, manages collections and supplier terms actively, and has handled a bank facility or covenant reporting.
criteria.anchor_5: Has taken a business through a cash squeeze with a forecast the owner trusted, renegotiated terms or facilities, and can show working capital days improving under their watch.
questions: Show me how you build a cash forecast. What goes wrong with it most often?
Tell me about a time cash was tight. What did you do in the first week?
How did you manage receivables in your last role, and what were the days at the start and end?

criteria.name: Compliance, tax and audit readiness
criteria.anchor_1: Files what the accountant tells them to file. Cannot describe the entity's tax and e invoicing obligations or the audit timetable.
criteria.anchor_3: Owns the compliance calendar (VAT, corporate tax, e invoicing, social insurance as applicable), has managed an audit end to end, and closes findings.
criteria.anchor_5: Has implemented a regulatory change (e invoicing phase, corporate tax introduction, a new filing regime) on time, has a clean audit history, and can explain the entity's exposure without notes.
evidence_sources: reference: engagement auditor or tax adviser
questions: List the filings this business makes in a year and who prepares each one.
Tell me about a regulatory change you implemented. What did it take and what nearly went wrong?
What was the last audit finding you received and how did you close it?

criteria.name: Systems, data and modelling
criteria.anchor_1: Uses the accounting system for entry only and builds reports by hand each month. Spreadsheets have no controls.
criteria.anchor_3: Configures the accounting system's reporting, builds models with clear structure and checks, and has automated recurring reports.
criteria.anchor_5: Has selected or implemented an accounting system or ERP module, builds models others can audit, and has removed manual steps from reporting with measurable effect.
evidence_sources: work sample: a model they built
questions: Show me a model you built. How does someone else check it?
What would you change about our accounting system in the first three months?
Describe a report you automated. What did it replace?

criteria.name: People and stakeholder management
criteria.anchor_1: Has not managed staff, or cannot describe how an owner or board was kept informed beyond sending reports.
criteria.anchor_3: Has managed a small team, deals directly with the owner, auditors, bank and tax adviser, and can describe a difficult conversation with each.
criteria.anchor_5: Is the person the owner calls first on any number, has built a team from one or two people, and has managed a bank, auditor or investor relationship through a difficult period.
questions: How do you keep an owner informed who does not read finance reports?
Tell me about a disagreement with an auditor or bank and how it was resolved.
Describe the team you managed and one person you developed.

criteria.name: Judgment and integrity under pressure
criteria.anchor_1: Cannot describe a situation where they were pressured on a number, or describes yielding without escalation.
criteria.anchor_3: Describes at least one situation where they held a position under pressure from an owner or manager, and documented it.
criteria.anchor_5: Describes a serious situation (a request to misstate, an undisclosed related party, a personal expense through the business) handled with a clear account of what they would and would not do. The reference confirms it.
questions: Tell me about a time you were asked to record something you did not agree with. What did you do?
In a family owned business, where is the line between the owner's money and the company's, and how do you hold it?
Describe a mistake in the numbers that was yours. How was it found and what did you do?
